docs.title: 🧩 Architectural Highlights
docs.text:
• Zero Data Egress

    All customer data stays entirely inside your warehouse security perimeter (DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks). Fully compliant with HIPAA, GDPR, and CCPA.

  • Deterministic & Auditable

    Every edge, cluster, and golden attribute is backed by explicit match rules and Spanning Tree Connectivity scoring. No probabilistic black-box hallucinations.

  • Anchor-Based Graph Building

    Avoids Cartesian join blowouts on common identifiers by connecting groups via star-topology anchor edges (O(N) complexity instead of O(N²)).

  • Incremental Delta Upsert

    Local Subgraph Stitching isolates only impacted clusters during incremental runs, updating 1.5M clusters in seconds without full historical table scans.

  • Zero-Retype Credentials

    Auto-detects active credentials from ~/.databrickscfg, ~/.snowflake/connections.toml, ~/.dbt/profiles.yml, and Google Cloud ADC with 1-click connect.

  • AI Agent Ready (MCP)

    Includes 17 FastMCP tools allowing Cursor, Claude Desktop, and Antigravity to autonomously profile schemas, simulate rule impact, and resolve Customer 360 records.

docs.text: SQL Identity Resolution (sql-identity-oss) is a warehouse-native, deterministic identity resolution and customer 360 engine designed for modern data platforms. docs.title: 1. Deterministic-First Graph Construction
docs.text:
• Matches entities using high-confidence identifiers (email, phone, loyalty_id, device_id, account_id).
  • Normalizes values on extraction (e.g., lowercasing, stripping whitespace, or custom SQL expressions).
  • Employs an anchor-based N-1 edge building strategy to link groups of entities in $O(N)$ edges rather than $O(N^2)$ cross-products.

docs.title: 2. High-Cardinality Safeguards
docs.text:
• Configurable max_group_size per rule prevents graph explosion from shared or placeholder identifiers (e.g. support@company.com, 000-000-0000).
  • Oversized groups are gracefully bypassed and logged to idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups for auditing.
  • Exact and wildcard blocklists (idr_meta.identifier_exclusion) filter out system accounts and junk values before edge formation.

docs.title: 3. Distributed Connected-Component Resolution
docs.text:
• Graph clusters are resolved in pure SQL via iterative Label Propagation.
  • Satisfies formal mathematical graph invariants:
  • Partition Completeness: Every entity belongs to exactly one cluster.
  • Connected-Component Completeness: 0 edges cross distinct clusters.
  • Minimum-Label Determinism: resolved_id is deterministically the minimum entity_key in the component.

docs.title: 4. Optional Probabilistic Refinement
docs.text:
• When --strict mode is disabled, optional fuzzy matching rules (e.g., Jaro-Winkler, Levenshtein, Metaphone) group resolved clusters into higher-level Super-Clusters (super_cluster_id).
  • Pre-filtering blocking keys ensure fuzzy string comparisons remain performant at scale.

docs.title: 5. Automated Golden Record Survivorship
docs.text:
• Constructs unified 360° customer profiles (idr_out.golden_profiles) according to declarative attribute survivorship strategies:
  • RECENCY: Most recent non-null value based on timestamp/watermark.
  • PRIORITY: Highest-ranked source system wins (e.g., CRM > POS > Web), with null-penalization.
  • FREQUENCY: Most common value across all cluster entities.

docs.title: ⚡ 1. The 60-Second Demo (Local DuckDB)
docs.text:
The quickest way to evaluate IDR is through the built-in zero-config quickstart.

# 1. Install IDR with DuckDB and MCP extras
pip install "sql-identity-resolution[duckdb,api,mcp]"

# 2. Run the quickstart command
idr quickstart

docs.title: What Happens Behind the Scenes:
docs.text:
1. Generates Synthetic Retail Data: Creates 10,000 realistic customer rows across 4 source systems (web, store, mobile, call_center) with realistic overlap in email, phone, and loyalty IDs.
  2. Initializes Schema: Provisions idr_meta, idr_work, and idr_out schemas in a local DuckDB file (quickstart_demo.duckdb).
  3. Applies Metadata Rules: Configures exact matching rules for EMAIL, PHONE, and LOYALTY, sets attribute mappings, and defines Golden Profile survivorship rules.
  4. Executes Identity Resolution: Runs FULL mode resolution with Label Propagation and materializes final identity tables.
  5. Prints Summary: Outputs duration, entities processed, edges formed, and cluster size distributions.

Customizing the quickstart: 

idr quickstart --rows=50000 --output=my_demo.duckdb --seed=123

docs.title: Querying with SQL
docs.text:
You can query the output tables directly using the DuckDB CLI or Python:

duckdb quickstart_demo.duckdb

-- See cluster size distribution
SELECT
    cluster_size,
    COUNT(*) as total_clusters,
    SUM(cluster_size) as total_entities
FROM idr_out.identity_clusters_current
GROUP BY cluster_size
ORDER BY cluster_size;

-- View resolved customer memberships
SELECT
    m.entity_key,
    m.resolved_id,
    c.cluster_size,
    c.confidence_score
FROM idr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current m
JOIN idr_out.identity_clusters_current c ON m.resolved_id = c.resolved_id
LIMIT 10;

-- Inspect Unified Golden Profiles
SELECT * FROM idr_out.golden_profiles LIMIT 5;

docs.title: Configuration Guide: Mental Model, Core Fields & Runtime Lifecycle
docs.text:
IDR configurations can be authored as a declarative YAML manifest (idr_config.yaml), configured visually through the 6-Step Web UI Setup Wizard (idr ui), or generated automatically by an AI agent via FastMCP (discover_and_suggest_rules).

Regardless of how you create it, the configuration defines four core concepts:

  1. Primary Keys (entity_key) — How to uniquely identify each raw row.
  2. Watermark Columns (watermark_column) — How to track incremental changes and recency.
  3. Identifiers (identifiers) — Which columns link records together into identity clusters.
  4. Attributes (attributes & survivorship) — Which columns populate the unified Golden Profile.

docs.title: 1. Primary Key (entity_key) & Source ID (id)
docs.text:
Every source table must specify a short id (e.g., "crm", "orders", "pos") and an entity_key column or SQL expression (e.g., "customer_id", "order_id").

  • Why it is required: Different source systems frequently use auto-incrementing integers (1, 2, 3...) that would collide if pooled together.
  • How the app uses it: During extraction, IDR combines id and entity_key into a globally unique composite node key formatted as <source_id>:<entity_key>:
  • Row 1042 in raw.crm_customers (id: "crm") becomes crm:1042
  • Row 1042 in raw.web_orders (id: "orders") becomes orders:1042
  • Deterministic Cluster ID (resolved_id): When multiple records merge into a cluster, IDR deterministically assigns the lexicographically smallest entity_key in that connected component (e.g., crm:1042) as the cluster's canonical resolved_id.

[!TIP] What if my table has a composite primary key? Because entity_key accepts safe SQL expressions, you can pass CONCAT(store_id, '-', transaction_id) if a table does not have a single-column primary key.

docs.title: 2. Identifiers vs. Attributes (What's the Difference?)
docs.text:
New users often ask why a column like email or phone can appear in both identifiers and attributes. They serve two completely different stages of the pipeline:

Concept Pipeline Stage Question It Answers Examples Output Table Impacted Identifiers (sources[].identifiers) Stage 2 & 3: Graph Edge Building "Do these two records belong to the same real-world person?" email, phone, loyalty_id, ssn, account_id idr_out.identity_edges_currentidr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current Attributes (sources[].attributes) Stage 5 & 6: Golden Profile & Survivorship "Now that these 5 records are merged, what is the customer's best name, email, and city?" first_name, last_name, email, phone, billing_city, vip_tier idr_out.golden_profiles
  • Rule of Thumb:
  • Put a column in identifiers ONLY if two records sharing that exact value should be linked together as the same person (never put first_name or city in identifiers, or every "John" will merge into one cluster!).
  • Put a column in attributes if you want that field to appear as a consolidated column on the final Golden Profile (idr_out.golden_profiles) or if a Fuzzy Rule needs to compare it within an already-blocked candidate pair.
  • Put email and phone in both if you want to link records by email/phone and want email_primary and phone_primary on your Golden Profile.

docs.title: 3. Watermark Column (watermark_column) & Why It Is Required
docs.text: Every source table defines a watermark_column (such as updated_at, modified_ts, order_date, or ingested_at).

docs.title: Why the App Requires It:
docs.text:
1. 90–99% Lower Warehouse Compute in Incremental Mode (--mode INCR):
  2. After every successful run, IDR records the maximum observed timestamp per source table in idr_meta.run_state (last_watermark_value).
  3. On the next incremental run, IDR automatically generates a delta filter: 
    WHERE updated_at > '<last_watermark_value>' - INTERVAL '<watermark_lookback_minutes> minutes'
  4. Instead of re-scanning 500 million historical rows, the warehouse only scans rows inserted or updated since the last run, then stitches those delta entities into existing clusters.
  5. Tie-Breaking in RECENCY Survivorship:
  6. Suppose crm:1 (updated in 2023) has phone 555-0100, and orders:99 (updated in 2026) has phone 555-0199.
  7. When constructing idr_out.golden_profiles, the RECENCY strategy orders candidate values by each source record's watermark/recency timestamp (ORDER BY record_updated_at DESC) so the customer's newest phone number wins.

[!NOTE] What if my table doesn't have an updated_at timestamp? * Use a creation/event timestamp column (created_at, order_date, signup_date). * If the table is a static snapshot with no date/timestamp column at all, always run in --mode FULL (full refresh) and use PRIORITY or FREQUENCY survivorship instead of RECENCY.

docs.text:
Whether you configure IDR via YAML (idr_config.yaml), the Web UI Setup Wizard, or FastMCP Agent tools, the application compiles your configuration into the idr_meta schema (or dbt_idr seed CSVs) and executes a 6-stage SQL pipeline:

docs.title: Stage-by-Stage Config Consumption Matrix
docs.text: Config Section Stored In (idr_meta / dbt_idr Seed) Consumed By Stage Exact SQL Behavior sources[].idsources[].tablesources[].entity_keysources[].watermark_column idr_meta.source_table(idr_sources.csv) Stage 1: Entity Extraction Queries each active table_fqn, applies the incremental watermark_column filter, and emits CONCAT('<id>', ':', CAST(<entity_key> AS VARCHAR)) into idr_work.entities_delta. sources[].identifiers idr_meta.identifier_mapping(idr_identifier_mappings.csv) Stage 2: Identifier Extraction Extracts each mapped column (email, phone, loyalty_id), applies LOWER() / UPPER() from rules[].canonicalize, and strips NULL or empty strings. exclusions[] idr_meta.identifier_exclusion(idr_exclusions.csv) Stage 2: Identifier Extraction Filters out known toxic placeholder values (EXACT or LIKE, e.g. test@%, 0000000000) before any graph joins occur. rules[] idr_meta.rule(idr_rules.csv) Stage 3: Edge Building Groups records sharing the same normalized identifier_type + identifier_value_norm. If a group has $> \text{max_group_size}$ entities, it is quarantined to idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups; otherwise, every member links to the group's minimum anchor_entity_key. fuzzy_rules[] idr_meta.fuzzy_rule Stage 5: Fuzzy Refinement Partitions clusters by blocking_key, evaluates dialect-specific score_expr (e.g., Jaro-Winkler), and links clusters scoring $\ge \text{threshold}$ via super_cluster_id (disabled when --strict is passed). sources[].attributessurvivorship[] idr_meta.entity_attribute_mappingidr_meta.survivorship_rule(idr_attribute_mappings.csv, idr_survivorship_rules.csv) Stage 6: Golden Profile Generation Joins all member records in each cluster and ranks non-null candidate values per attribute using window functions (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY resolved_id ORDER BY ...)), outputting the winning values to idr_out.golden_profiles.

docs.title: 📄 Complete Annotated Example Manifest
docs.text:
sources:
  - id: "crm"                           # Short prefix -> produces entity_keys like "crm:1001"
    table: "raw.crm_customers"          # Warehouse table FQN (schema.table or catalog.schema.table)
    entity_key: "customer_id"           # Unique primary key column in raw.crm_customers
    entity_type: "PERSON"
    watermark_column: "updated_at"      # Used for incremental (INCR) delta filtering & RECENCY tie-breaking
    watermark_lookback_minutes: 0       # Optional safety buffer for late-arriving streaming data
    identifiers:                        # Columns used to LINK records together into clusters
      - type: "email"
        expr: "email"
      - type: "phone"
        expr: "phone"
      - type: "loyalty"
        expr: "loyalty_id"
    attributes:                         # Columns carried into the final Golden Profile (Customer 360)
      - name: "first_name"
        expr: "first_name"
      - name: "last_name"
        expr: "last_name"
      - name: "email"
        expr: "email"
      - name: "phone"
        expr: "phone"

  - id: "web"                           # Produces entity_keys like "web:5009"
    table: "raw.web_users"
    entity_key: "user_id"
    entity_type: "PERSON"
    watermark_column: "last_login_ts"
    identifiers:
      - type: "email"
        expr: "user_email"              # Maps source column `user_email` -> semantic identifier `email`
      - type: "phone"
        expr: "mobile_phone"            # Maps source column `mobile_phone` -> semantic identifier `phone`
    attributes:
      - name: "first_name"
        expr: "first_name"
      - name: "last_name"
        expr: "last_name"
      - name: "email"
        expr: "user_email"

rules:
  - id: "r_email"
    type: "EXACT"
    match_keys: ["email"]               # Links any records sharing the `email` identifier type
    canonicalize: "LOWERCASE"           # Normalizes 'Alice@Example.com' -> 'alice@example.com'
    priority: 1
    max_group_size: 100                 # Guardrail: skips shared emails appearing on >100 records

  - id: "r_phone"
    type: "EXACT"
    match_keys: ["phone"]
    canonicalize: "EXACT"
    priority: 2
    max_group_size: 5000

  - id: "r_loyalty"
    type: "EXACT"
    match_keys: ["loyalty"]
    canonicalize: "EXACT"
    priority: 3
    max_group_size: 1000

fuzzy_rules:
  - id: "fuzzy_last_name"
    name: "Fuzzy Last Name within Soundex Block"
    blocking_key: "SUBSTRING(last_name, 1, 3)"
    score_expr:
      duckdb: "jaro_winkler_similarity(a.last_name, b.last_name)"
      snowflake: "JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY(a.last_name, b.last_name) / 100.0"
      bigquery: "1.0 - (EDIT_DISTANCE(a.last_name, b.last_name) / GREATEST(LENGTH(a.last_name), LENGTH(b.last_name), 1))"
      databricks: "jaro_winkler(a.last_name, b.last_name)"
    threshold: 0.85
    priority: 10

survivorship:
  - attribute: "first_name"
    strategy: "PRIORITY"                # Prefer CRM over Web for first_name (skips NULLs automatically)
    source_priority: ["crm", "web"]

  - attribute: "last_name"
    strategy: "RECENCY"                 # Pick the most recently updated non-null last_name
    recency_field: "updated_at"

  - attribute: "email"
    strategy: "RECENCY"
    recency_field: "updated_at"

  - attribute: "phone"
    strategy: "FREQUENCY"               # Pick the most common phone value across the cluster

exclusions:
  - identifier_type: "email"
    value: "support@company.com"
    match_type: "EXACT"
    reason: "Internal support ticketing inbox"

  - identifier_type: "email"
    value: "%@noreply.example.com"
    match_type: "LIKE"
    reason: "Automated notification domain"

docs.title: 1. sources
docs.text:
Defines source tables to ingest into the identity graph.

Field Type Required Description id string Yes Unique source prefix (used in entity_key prefixing, lineage, and PRIORITY survivorship). table string Yes Fully-qualified table name (schema.table or catalog.schema.table). entity_key string Yes Unique primary key column or SQL expression in the source table. entity_type string No Entity categorization (default: "PERSON"). watermark_column string No Timestamp/date column used for incremental delta filtering (INCR mode) and RECENCY survivorship (default: "updated_at"). watermark_lookback_minutes integer No Buffer window (minutes) for late-arriving records (default: 0). identifiers list Yes List of identifier mappings (type, expr, is_hashed) used to build matching edges. attributes list No List of profile attributes (name, expr) used to build idr_out.golden_profiles.

docs.title: 2. rules (Deterministic Matching)
docs.text:
Exact matching rules that form graph edges.

Field Type Default Description id string Required Unique rule ID. type string "EXACT" Match type. match_keys list Required Identifier types that must match (e.g. ["email"]). canonicalize string "LOWERCASE" Value normalization: "LOWERCASE", "UPPERCASE", or "EXACT" / "NONE". priority integer 100 Rule priority (lower number = higher edge priority in evidence). max_group_size integer 10000 High-cardinality guardrail. Groups larger than this are skipped and logged to idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups.

docs.title: 3. fuzzy_rules (Probabilistic Super-Clustering)
docs.text:
Optional refinement rules executed when --strict is not enabled.

Field Type Description id string Unique fuzzy rule ID. name string Human-readable rule description. blocking_key string SQL expression partitioning candidates before cross-comparison (e.g., soundex or first 3 characters). score_expr string or dict Similarity score expression yielding 0.0 to 1.0. Can be a string or a dialect-keyed dictionary (duckdb, snowflake, bigquery, databricks). threshold float Minimum score (0.0 to 1.0) required to merge clusters into a Super-Cluster. priority integer Execution priority.

[!TIP] In the Web UI Setup Wizard, choosing a fuzzy template (Jaro-Winkler, Levenshtein, Soundex) automatically substitutes {col} with your selected attribute and selects the target warehouse's native function.

docs.title: 4. survivorship (Golden Record Resolution)
docs.text:
Controls how attributes from multiple source records within a cluster are consolidated into idr_out.golden_profiles.

Strategy Description Required Parameters RECENCY Selects the non-null value from the record with the most recent timestamp. recency_field (or defaults to source watermark_column) PRIORITY Selects the value from the highest-ranked source system. Automatically skips NULL values. source_priority (ordered list of source ids) FREQUENCY Selects the most frequently occurring non-null value across all cluster members (tie-broken by recency). None

docs.title: 5. exclusions (Identifier Blocklist)
docs.text:
Blocks specific placeholder or shared values from linking records to prevent hub-and-spoke false clustering.

Field Type Description identifier_type string Identifier type to filter (e.g. email, phone). value string Value or pattern to block. match_type string "EXACT" (exact string match) or "LIKE" (SQL wildcard matching with %). reason string Optional description for auditing.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: The idr command-line interface is the primary operational tool for configuring, provisioning, and executing SQL Identity Resolution pipelines across DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, and Databricks.

docs.title: 🛠️ Global Usage
docs.text: idr [--help] <command> [options]

docs.title: Commands Summary
docs.text: Command Description idr ui Launch the interactive IDR Studio UI & API server in one command (opens browser automatically) idr run Execute full or incremental identity resolution pipelines (--platform auto-detected if omitted) idr init Provision or reset system schemas (idr_meta, idr_work, idr_out) idr config Validate, generate SQL DDL, apply YAML configurations, or export to dbt_idr seeds idr dbt export Export YAML or live warehouse metadata directly into the 6 standard dbt_idr seed CSVs idr quickstart Generate synthetic multi-channel retail data and run an automated local demo idr mcp / idr-mcp Start the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI assistants (19 tools) idr serve Launch the FastAPI REST service, bundled UI, and Prometheus metrics endpoint idr version Print current package and engine version

docs.title: 1. idr run
docs.text:
Executes the 6-stage identity resolution pipeline against your target warehouse.

idr run --platform=<platform> [connection-flags] [options]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Flag Type Default Description --platform -p String Auto-detected Target warehouse: duckdb, snowflake, bigquery, or databricks (inferred from --db, --project, IDR_PLATFORM, or local credentials if omitted) --mode -m String FULL Pipeline execution mode: FULL (complete rebuild) or INCR (delta watermarks) --config Path None Path to declarative YAML configuration to apply prior to run --max-iters Integer 30 Maximum iterations for distributed label propagation --dry-run Flag False Computes cluster impact and diffs without mutating production tables --strict Flag False Deterministic mode: strictly disable fuzzy similarity matching

docs.title: Warehouse Connection Flags
docs.text:
• DuckDB:
  • --db PATH: Path to local DuckDB database file (e.g. --db=analytics.duckdb).
  • BigQuery:
  • --project ID: Google Cloud project ID.
  • --location: BigQuery dataset region (default: US).
  • --dataset: Output dataset name (default: idr_out).
  • --meta-dataset: Metadata dataset name (default: idr_meta).
  • --work-dataset: Working dataset name (default: idr_work).
  • Snowflake:
  • Configured via environment variables (SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT, SNOWFLAKE_USER, SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD, SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE, SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE, SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA) or standard Snowflake connection profile (~/.snowflake/connections.toml).
  • Databricks:
  • Configured via environment variables (DATABRICKS_HOST, DATABRICKS_TOKEN, DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Run full resolution on local DuckDB
idr run --platform=duckdb --db=demo.duckdb --mode=FULL

# Incremental run on Snowflake with strict deterministic matching
idr run --platform=snowflake --mode=INCR --strict

# Dry-run analysis on BigQuery with custom YAML configuration
idr run --platform=bigquery --project=my-gcp-project --config=idr_config.yaml --dry-run

docs.title: 2. idr init
docs.text:
Initializes metadata tables and serving schema DDL in the target warehouse.

idr init --platform=<platform> [connection-flags] [--reset]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --platform String Required Target warehouse (duckdb, snowflake, bigquery, databricks) --reset Flag False Destructive: Drops and recreates existing metadata tables

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# Initialize schema on Databricks
idr init --platform=databricks

# Reset local DuckDB schemas
idr init --platform=duckdb --db=test.duckdb --reset

docs.title: 3. idr config
docs.text: Manage, validate, and generate SQL from declarative YAML configurations.

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text:
• idr config validate --file=<path>: Validates syntax, schema definitions, and survivorship rules against the IDR configuration specification.
idr config validate --file=config/retail_rules.yaml
  • idr config generate --file=<path> [--dialect=<dialect>]: Translates declarative YAML configuration into dialect-specific SQL DDL/DML statements (duckdb, snowflake, bigquery, databricks).
idr config generate --file=rules.yaml --dialect=snowflake > deploy_rules.sql
  • idr config apply --file=<path> [--platform=<platform>] [connection-flags]: Executes generated SQL statements directly against your target warehouse to update metadata tables.
idr config apply --file=rules.yaml --db=demo.duckdb
  • idr dbt export (or idr config export-dbt): Compiles a YAML configuration file (--file) or live warehouse idr_meta tables (--db / --platform) into the 6 standard dbt_idr seed CSV files (idr_sources.csv, idr_identifier_mappings.csv, idr_attribute_mappings.csv, idr_rules.csv, idr_exclusions.csv, idr_survivorship_rules.csv).
# Export from YAML manifest to your dbt project's seeds directory
idr dbt export --file=idr_config.yaml --output-dir=dbt_idr/seeds

# Export from live DuckDB metadata tables configured via the Web UI
idr dbt export --db=demo.duckdb --output-dir=dbt_idr/seeds

docs.title: Platforms & Connectivity
docs.text: IDR provides first-class, native SQL engine parity across 4 major data warehouse platforms. All core logic (extraction, edge building, label propagation, fuzzy matching, and survivorship) runs entirely inside the data warehouse.

docs.title: 🦆 DuckDB (Local & In-Memory)
docs.text: Ideal for local testing, rapid CI/CD runs, and embedded edge workloads (< 10M rows).

• File Database: Local file path (e.g. production.duckdb).

idr init --platform duckdb --db production.duckdb

• Set memory limits for massive local datasets: 

    SET memory_limit = '16GB';
SET threads = 8;

docs.text:
• Cluster Keys: For tables with >10M rows, cluster identity tables for fast lookups:

ALTER TABLE idr_out.identity_identifiers_current CLUSTER BY (identifier_type);

Authenticate via Google Application Default Credentials (ADC) or service account key:

export IDR_PROJECT="my-gcp-project-id"

idr init --platform bigquery --project $IDR_PROJECT

# Apply configuration

# Execute resolution
idr run --platform bigquery --project $IDR_PROJECT --mode FULL

docs.title: BigQuery-Specific Considerations
docs.text:
• Column Types: BigQuery uses STRING, INT64, FLOAT64, TIMESTAMP, and BOOL.
  • Primary Keys: BigQuery primary keys are defined as NOT ENFORCED.
  • String Hashing: Uses TO_HEX(SHA256(CAST(expr AS STRING))).
  • Dataset Location: Datasets default to US unless specified via --location.

docs.title: 🧱 Databricks (Delta Lake / Unity Catalog)
docs.text:
Distributed data lakehouse powered by Apache Spark and Delta Lake.

Databricks Testing & Walkthrough Guide

Follow our step-by-step Databricks Testing Guide for running on Databricks Free Tier (Community Edition or 14-Day Cloud Trial).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install "sql-identity-resolution[databricks]"

docs.title: Authentication & Environment Variables
docs.text:
IDR connects via the official databricks-sql-connector to SQL Warehouses (Serverless or Classic) or All-Purpose Clusters:

export DATABRICKS_HOST="dbc-abcdef-1234.cloud.databricks.com"
export DATABRICKS_TOKEN="dapi1234567890abcdef"
export DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH="/sql/1.0/warehouses/abcdef1234567890"

docs.title: CLI Execution
docs.text:
# Initialize schemas
idr init --platform databricks

# Apply configuration
idr config apply --platform databricks --file config.yaml

# Execute resolution
idr run --platform databricks --mode FULL

docs.title: Delta Lake & Unity Catalog Optimizations
docs.text:
• Column Defaults Compatibility: IDR DDL automatically omits DEFAULT constraints on Databricks Delta tables. This avoids the [WRONG_COLUMN_DEFAULTS_FOR_DELTA_FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED] error on Delta tables without requiring custom TBLPROPERTIES.
  • Table Swapping: Internal stage table swaps use transactional CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ... AS SELECT * FROM ... + DROP TABLE, avoiding cross-schema rename issues in Unity Catalog.
  • Table Maintenance: Periodically optimize and vacuum identity tables: 
    OPTIMIZE idr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current ZORDER BY (resolved_id);
OPTIMIZE idr_out.identity_edges_current ZORDER BY (identifier_type);

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Cloud Dialects
docs.text:
To run the automated smoke test suite against your live cloud instances, set the credentials above and run:

pytest tests/test_cloud_dialects_live.py -v

This test dynamically verifies schema initialization, data ingestion, FULL resolution, DRY_RUN validation, and Golden Profile survivorship against your live warehouse.

docs.title: Pipeline Deep Dive
docs.text: The runner orchestrates four stages: preflight, extraction, graph, and output.

docs.title: 1. Preflight
docs.text:
• Checks for concurrent runs.
  • Verifies source tables exist.
  • Applies schema upgrades (best-effort).
  • Validates identifier mappings against actual columns.

docs.title: 2. Extraction
docs.text:
• Builds idr_work.entities_delta based on watermarks (FULL or INCR).
  • Extracts identifiers into idr_work.identifiers_all.
  • Extracts attributes into idr_work.entity_attributes for fuzzy and survivorship.
  • Applies exclusions from idr_meta.identifier_exclusion if present.

docs.title: 3. Graph
docs.text:
• Builds edges with an anchor-based N-1 approach (avoids O(N^2)).
  • Skips identifier groups larger than max_group_size.
  • Label propagation resolves connected components into clusters.
  • Optional fuzzy matching builds super-clusters (skipped in --strict).

docs.title: 4. Output
docs.text:
• Upserts membership, edges, and clusters.
  • Computes confidence scores (edge diversity + match density).
  • Updates watermarks in idr_meta.run_state.
  • Builds golden profiles via ProfileBuilder.

docs.title: Dry run mode
docs.text:
• Runs all stages but writes to idr_out.dry_run_results and idr_out.dry_run_summary.
  • Does not modify production tables.

docs.title: Schema & Data Model Reference
docs.text:
IDR organizes all state into three schemas across all 4 supported data warehouses:

  1. idr_meta: Configuration, rules, mappings, and watermarks.
  2. idr_work: Transient staging tables used during pipeline execution.
  3. idr_out: Production identity graph, resolved clusters, golden profiles, and telemetry.

docs.title: idr_meta.source_table
docs.text:
Registry of source tables to be ingested.

Column Type Primary Key Description table_id STRING PK Unique identifier for source table (e.g. crm, pos). table_fqn STRING Fully qualified table name (schema.table or catalog.schema.table). entity_type STRING Entity category (e.g. PERSON, ACCOUNT). entity_key_expr STRING SQL expression producing the source entity key. watermark_column STRING Timestamp/date column used for incremental watermark tracking. watermark_lookback_minutes INT Lookback buffer window in minutes for late-arriving records. is_active BOOLEAN Whether this source table is processed during pipeline execution.

docs.title: idr_meta.rule
docs.text:
Deterministic matching rules.

Column Type Primary Key Description rule_id STRING PK Unique rule identifier (e.g. r_email). identifier_type STRING Standardized identifier type to match (e.g. EMAIL, PHONE). canonicalize STRING Normalization strategy (LOWERCASE, UPPERCASE, or EXACT). max_group_size INT Guardrail limit. Groups larger than this are skipped. priority INT Execution and evidence ranking priority (lower = higher priority). is_active BOOLEAN Whether this rule is enabled.

docs.title: idr_meta.identifier_mapping
docs.text:
Maps source table columns/expressions to standardized identifier types.

Column Type Primary Key Description table_id STRING PK Foreign key to source_table.table_id. identifier_type STRING PK Identifier category (e.g. EMAIL, PHONE, LOYALTY). identifier_value_expr STRING SQL expression extracting the raw identifier value. is_hashed BOOLEAN Whether source values are already hashed (e.g. SHA-256).

docs.title: idr_meta.entity_attribute_mapping
docs.text:
Maps source columns to profile attributes for Golden Profile survivorship.

Column Type Primary Key Description table_id STRING PK Foreign key to source_table.table_id. attribute_name STRING PK Standardized profile attribute name (e.g. first_name, email). attribute_expr STRING SQL expression extracting the attribute value.

docs.title: idr_meta.survivorship_rule
docs.text:
Rules for resolving Golden Profile attribute values.

Column Type Primary Key Description attribute_name STRING PK Target profile attribute. strategy STRING Survivorship strategy: RECENCY, PRIORITY, or FREQUENCY. source_priority_list STRING JSON list of prioritized table_ids for PRIORITY strategy. recency_field STRING Optional source timestamp field for RECENCY strategy. is_active BOOLEAN Enabled status.

docs.title: idr_meta.fuzzy_rule
docs.text:
Probabilistic matching rules (used when --strict is not enabled).

Column Type Primary Key Description rule_id STRING PK Unique fuzzy rule ID. rule_name STRING Descriptive rule name. blocking_key_expr STRING SQL expression partitioning records before similarity comparisons. score_expr STRING Dialect-appropriate similarity expression returning 0.0 to 1.0. threshold DOUBLE Minimum score required to merge clusters. priority INT Execution priority. is_active BOOLEAN Enabled status.

docs.title: idr_meta.identifier_exclusion
docs.text:
Blocklist for filtering out placeholder, system, or generic identifiers.

Column Type Primary Key Description identifier_type STRING PK Identifier type (e.g. EMAIL, PHONE). identifier_value_pattern STRING PK Exact string or SQL wildcard pattern (%). match_type STRING EXACT or LIKE. reason STRING Audit reason (e.g. "Shared store tablet").

docs.title: idr_meta.run_state
docs.text:
Tracks high-watermarks for incremental processing.

Column Type Primary Key Description table_id STRING PK Source table ID. last_watermark_value TIMESTAMP Highest watermark processed in last successful run. last_run_id STRING ID of the run that updated this watermark. updated_at TIMESTAMP Timestamp of state update.

docs.title: idr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current
docs.text:
Maps every source entity to its resolved Identity Cluster ID.

Column Type Primary Key Description entity_key STRING PK Unique entity key ({table_id}:{source_key}). resolved_id STRING The resolved Identity Cluster ID (minimum entity key in cluster). run_id STRING ID of the run that produced or updated this membership. super_cluster_id STRING Higher-level cluster ID if merged by probabilistic fuzzy matching. updated_at TIMESTAMP Timestamp when membership was materialized.

docs.title: idr_out.identity_clusters_current
docs.text:
Master list of active identity clusters with quality and confidence metrics.

Column Type Primary Key Description resolved_id STRING PK Unique Cluster ID. cluster_size INT Count of member entities in this cluster. run_id STRING ID of the run that updated this cluster. super_cluster_id STRING Higher-level fuzzy cluster ID. confidence_score DOUBLE Composite quality score (0.0 to 1.0) based on edge diversity and density. primary_reason STRING Explanation of the confidence score. updated_at TIMESTAMP Last update timestamp.

docs.title: idr_out.identity_edges_current
docs.text:
Graph edges representing direct links between entities.

Column Type Primary Key Description left_entity_key STRING PK Source entity A. right_entity_key STRING PK Source entity B. identifier_type STRING PK Identifier type that formed the link. identifier_value_norm STRING Normalized matching value. first_seen_ts TIMESTAMP Timestamp when edge was first observed. last_seen_ts TIMESTAMP Timestamp when edge was most recently confirmed. run_id STRING Run ID that created/updated the edge.

docs.title: idr_out.identity_identifiers_current
docs.text:
Current registry of all entity identifiers for fast incremental candidate expansion.

Column Type Primary Key Description entity_key STRING PK Source entity key. identifier_type STRING PK Standardized identifier type. identifier_value_norm STRING Normalized value. is_hashed BOOLEAN Whether value was pre-hashed. run_id STRING Last update run ID. updated_at TIMESTAMP Last update timestamp.

docs.title: idr_out.golden_profiles
docs.text:

docs.title: 🧙‍♂️ 1. Setup Wizard (/setup)
docs.text:
The 6-step guided wizard configures and tests your entire identity resolution workflow without manual SQL or YAML editing.

flowchart TD
    S1["1. Connect<br/>(Warehouse Credentials & Validation)"] --> S2["2. Discover<br/>(Schema Discovery & Table Inspection)"]
    S2 --> S3["3. Map<br/>(Identifiers, Entity Keys & Attributes)"]
    S3 --> S4["4. Rules<br/>(Matching Rules, Priorities & Safeguards)"]
    S4 --> S5["5. Survivorship<br/>(Golden Attribute Survivorship Strategies)"]
    S5 --> S6["6. Review & Run<br/>(Dry-Run Scorecard & Live Pipeline Run)"]

docs.title: Step 1: Connect
docs.text:
• Select your target warehouse platform (DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks).
  • Provide connection parameters (e.g., file path, warehouse name, service account key, or Databricks host/token).
  • Verifies live connectivity before allowing you to proceed.

docs.title: Step 2: Discover
docs.text:
• Select the database schema where your raw tables live.
  • View discovered tables and preview schemas and column types.
  • Check the source tables you want to include in identity resolution.

docs.title: Step 3: Map Identifiers & Attributes
docs.text:
For each selected table, configure four core mappings (see Configuration Guide for the complete mental model):

  • Entity Key (Primary Key): The unique row identifier column in the source table (e.g., customer_id, order_id). IDR prefixes this with the table ID (crm:1042) so keys across different tables never collide.
  • Watermark Column: A timestamp or date column (updated_at, order_date) used for two purposes:
  • Incremental Runs (INCR mode): Only scans rows modified since the previous run's watermark, saving 90–99% of warehouse compute.
  • RECENCY Survivorship: Determines which record holds the newest attribute value when building the Golden Profile.
  • Identifiers (Graph Link Keys): Columns used to match and link records together into identity clusters (EMAIL, PHONE, LOYALTY_ID). Mark pre-hashed values if already SHA-256 encoded.
  • Attributes (Golden Profile Fields): Columns carried forward into idr_out.golden_profiles (e.g., first_name, last_name, email, phone, city) to construct the winning Customer 360 record after clusters are resolved.

docs.title: Step 4: Matching Rules & Exclusions
docs.text:
• Configure deterministic exact matching rules (EXACT) and assign priorities and max_group_size limits.
  • Fuzzy Attribute Selector: Choose a fuzzy similarity template (Jaro-Winkler, Levenshtein, Metaphone), select the target comparison attribute, and the UI automatically substitutes {col} into the warehouse-native similarity expression.
  • Identifier Exclusions Editor: Interactively add exact values or wildcard patterns (%@noreply.com) to prevent false-linkage hubs.

docs.title: Step 5: Golden Profile Survivorship
docs.text:
• Configure survivorship strategies per attribute:
  • RECENCY: Latest timestamp wins.
  • PRIORITY: Rank source tables in priority order (e.g. CRM > POS > Web). Automatically ignores NULL values.
  • FREQUENCY: Most common value across cluster members wins.

docs.title: Step 6: Review, Dry-Run & Execution
docs.text:
• View a unified summary of all configured sources, rules, and survivorship strategies.
  • Accurate Dry-Run Impact Breakdown: Execute a dry-run to preview proposed entity migrations before committing changes. Displays exact counts for:
  • Proposed Changes (New Entities + Moved Clusters)
  • Unchanged Entities
  • Total Entities
  • Click Run Pipeline to execute full resolution.

docs.title: 🔍 2. Identity Explorer (/explorer)
docs.text:
Investigate resolved customer identities, cluster structures, and unified profiles.

  • Unified Search: Search by email, phone number, loyalty ID, or entity key. Searches across both multi-entity clusters and singleton entities (entities with no links).
  • Golden Profile Banner: Displays the consolidated 360° customer profile directly above the cluster graph.
  • Interactive Graph Visualization: Visualizes entities as nodes connected by colored edge lines representing the matching rules that linked them.
  • Fuzzy Super-Clusters: Badges indicate if the cluster belongs to a broader probabilistic Super-Cluster (super_cluster_id).
  • Entity Member Table: Lists every source record with its source system, entity key, and attribute values.

docs.title: 📊 3. Operational Dashboard (/dashboard)
docs.text:
• High-Level Metrics: Total Entities Processed, Active Identity Clusters, Edges Formed, and Average Confidence Score.
  • Cluster Size Distribution: Interactive histogram showing singletons, pairs, small groups (3-5), and large clusters.
  • Rule Performance: Tracks how many edges each deterministic rule produced.
  • Quality Alerts: Flags high-cardinality groups or unusual cluster growth.

docs.title: ⏱️ 4. Pipeline Runs & Stage Drill-Down (/runs)
docs.text:
• Complete execution history across FULL, INCR, and DRY_RUN modes.
  • Expandable Stage Telemetry: Click any run row to view a detailed breakdown of each processing stage (preflight, entity_extraction, identifier_extraction, attribute_extraction, edge_building, label_propagation, fuzzy_matching, output_generation):
  • Per-stage duration (seconds)
  • Rows affected / produced
  • Label propagation iterations to convergence
  • Operational warnings or error messages

docs.title: REST API Reference
docs.text:
The IDR backend provides a comprehensive FastAPI REST API powering the Web UI, automated CI/CD pipelines, and external integrations.

  • Base URL: http://localhost:8000
  • Interactive Swagger UI: http://localhost:8000/docs
  • OpenAPI Schema: http://localhost:8000/openapi.json

docs.title: 1. Setup & Configuration (/api/setup)
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description POST /api/setup/connect Connect to a database adapter (duckdb, snowflake, bigquery, databricks). Initializes the session connection. GET /api/setup/status Check current connection and metadata initialization status. GET /api/setup/config Retrieve current saved configuration (sources, rules, survivorship, fuzzy rules, exclusions). POST /api/setup/config/save Validate and persist configuration to metadata tables (idr_meta). Requires write access in enterprise RBAC. GET /api/setup/discover/tables Discover tables in a given schema. Query param: ?schema=.... GET /api/setup/discover/columns Retrieve columns and data types for a table. Query param: ?table=.... GET /api/setup/fuzzy-templates Get supported fuzzy matching templates per dialect with parameter slots. POST /api/setup/run Trigger an identity resolution pipeline run (FULL, INCR, or dry_run=True).

docs.title: Example: Running a Pipeline via API
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/setup/run \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "mode": "FULL",
    "strict": false,
    "max_iterations": 30,
    "dry_run": false
  }'

docs.title: 2. Metrics & Dashboard (/api/metrics)
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description GET /api/metrics/summary Get high-level graph metrics: total entities, total clusters, total edges, and average confidence score. GET /api/metrics/distribution Get cluster size distribution bucketed into singletons, pairs, small, and large groups. GET /api/metrics/rules Get edge counts and active status broken down by matching rule. GET /api/alerts List operational and data quality alerts (e.g. skipped identifier groups, un-converged runs).

docs.title: 3. Identity Explorer (/api/entities & /api/clusters)
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description GET /api/entities/search?q={query} Search entities by identifier (email, phone, loyalty ID, entity key). Supports both cluster members and singletons. GET /api/clusters/{resolved_id} Retrieve comprehensive cluster details: member entities, connecting edges with rules, fuzzy super_cluster_id, and unified Golden Profile.

docs.title: 4. Pipeline Runs & Telemetry (/api/runs)
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description GET /api/runs List execution history with run mode, status, duration, entities processed, and warnings. GET /api/runs/{run_id} Retrieve deep stage telemetry (stage_metrics) for a specific run, including per-stage durations, row counts, and error details.

docs.title: 5. Enterprise Observability (/metrics & /api/auth)
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description GET /metrics Prometheus metrics scrape endpoint exporting idr_entities_processed_total, idr_edges_created_total, idr_clusters_impacted_total, and idr_last_run_duration_seconds. GET /api/health Health check endpoint returning { "status": "healthy" }. GET /api/auth/me Current authenticated user identity and RBAC roles (when OIDC is enabled).

docs.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server
docs.text:
The IDR MCP Server connects your identity graph directly to AI assistants such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, or custom LLM agent workflows using the open Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Agents can inspect clusters, trace edge evidence, query Golden Profiles, review run history, and dry-run pipeline executions using natural language.

docs.title: 🚀 Starting the MCP Server
docs.text:
# Environment Configuration
export IDR_PLATFORM=duckdb              # duckdb | snowflake | bigquery | databricks
export IDR_DATABASE=./demo.duckdb        # or Snowflake/BigQuery/Databricks credentials
export IDR_PII_ACCESS=masked            # "masked" (default) or "full"

# Start in stdio mode (for Claude Desktop / Cursor)
idr mcp

docs.title: 🔒 PII Masking & Privacy Controls
docs.text:
By default (IDR_PII_ACCESS=masked or unset), the MCP server automatically redacts sensitive attributes (emails, phone numbers, names):

  • john.doe@example.com becomes jo***om
  • 555-0199 becomes 55***99

To grant agents full unmasked access for internal audited workflows: 

export IDR_PII_ACCESS=full

docs.title: 1. Agentic Identity Intelligence & Customer 360 (New in v0.6.0)
docs.text:
• resolve_customer_360(identifier_value: str, identifier_type: str = None)
  • Primary context-grounding tool for AI agents and RAG pipelines. Given any fragmented customer identifier (email, phone, loyalty ID), resolves the person's canonical identity in a single call. Returns their unified Golden Profile attributes, all linked source accounts (e.g. CRM, Shopify, Zendesk), complete cross-channel identifier graph, and cluster confidence score.
  • discover_and_suggest_rules(table_fqn: str = None, sample_size: int = 500)
  • Autonomous data engineering tool. Inspects warehouse schemas, samples column data, semantically detects PII candidates (email, phone, account_id, loyalty_id, device_id), and automatically generates a production-ready declarative IDR YAML configuration with exact matching rules, max_group_size safeguards, and survivorship policies.
  • simulate_rule_impact(rule: Dict[str, Any], dialect: str = None)
  • Safe rule tuning & risk analysis. Takes a candidate matching rule and tests it against existing warehouse records without mutating production tables. Evaluates simulated anchor edge volume, predicted cluster merges, and flags supernode risks before deployment.

docs.title: 2. Cluster Investigation & Explanation
docs.text:
• explain_cluster(resolved_id: str)
  • Generates a comprehensive 360° explanation for a resolved cluster: cluster metadata (size, confidence score, primary reason, fuzzy super_cluster_id), member entities, connecting edges with rules, and the unified Golden Profile in a single call.
  • get_cluster(resolved_id: str, include_edges: bool = False, include_entities: bool = False)
  • Retrieves raw cluster metadata with optional inclusion of member entities and connecting edges.
  • get_golden_profile(resolved_id: str)
  • Retrieves the consolidated 360° customer profile for a cluster resulting from survivorship rules.
  • search_identifier(value: str, identifier_type: str = None, limit: int = 10)
  • Case-insensitive search for clusters matching an identifier (email, phone, loyalty ID). Finds both multi-entity clusters and singleton entities.

docs.title: 3. Edge & Evidence Reasoning
docs.text:
• explain_edge(entity_key_a: str, entity_key_b: str)
  • Discovers the exact evidence trail explaining why two entities are linked. Detects both direct connections (shared identifier and rule) and transitive connections (connected via intermediate entities in the same cluster).
  • list_edges_for_cluster(resolved_id: str, limit: int = 50)
  • Lists all internal graph edges connecting members within a resolved cluster.

docs.title: 4. Operational & Health Metrics
docs.text:
• get_metrics_summary()
  • High-level identity resolution graph telemetry: total clusters, total entities, total edges, and average cluster confidence score.
  • list_skipped_groups(limit: int = 20)
  • Audits high-cardinality identifier groups that were skipped by max_group_size guardrails to prevent hub flattening.
  • latest_run()
  • Returns status, duration, and metrics for the most recent pipeline run.
  • run_history(limit: int = 10)
  • Retrieves recent execution history across FULL, INCR, and DRY_RUN runs.

docs.title: 5. Configuration & Dry-Run Planning
docs.text:
• dry_run_pipeline(run_mode: str = "FULL", max_iters: int = 30)
  • Executes a dry-run analysis to preview proposed entity additions and cluster moves without mutating production tables.
  • list_rules()
  • Lists active deterministic matching rules and their priorities.
  • list_sources()
  • Lists active source tables, entity keys, and watermark columns.
  • config_snapshot(config_hash: str = None)
  • Retrieves the saved configuration JSON snapshot for historical auditing and reproducibility.

docs.text:
The dbt package provides deterministic-only identity resolution using SQL models.

  - git: "https://github.com/anilkulkarni87/sql-identity-resolution"
    subdirectory: "dbt_idr"

docs.title: Scale Testing & Graph Benchmarks
docs.text: IDR is engineered to process hundreds of millions of records inside data warehouses using set-based SQL and distributed graph algorithms.

docs.title: ⚡ Automated 260,000-Entity Benchmark
docs.text: IDR includes an end-to-end multi-source scale test script validating full resolution, incremental processing, and MCP agent responsiveness.

docs.title: Running the Benchmark
docs.text: python tools/scale_test/run_scale_and_mcp_benchmark.py --rows 250000 --incr-rows 10000

docs.title: Benchmark Architecture:
docs.text:
1. Multi-Source Generation: Generates 250,000 entities across 3 distinct source tables (CRM Accounts, Web Users, POS Customers) with natural overlapping identifiers.
  2. Deterministic & Guardrail Execution: Applies rules across EMAIL, PHONE, and LOYALTY, with max_group_size=100 catching a synthetic shared kiosk email.
  3. FULL Pipeline Run: Resolves 250,000 entities into 58,000+ clusters in 5 Label Propagation iterations at ~50,000 entities/sec.
  4. INCR Pipeline Run: Processes 10,000 newly arriving incremental rows in 1.5s, linking them to existing clusters without reprocessing the full graph.
  5. Graph Invariant Verification: Validates all 4 mathematical invariants:
  6. Partition Invariant: Every entity belongs to exactly one cluster (COUNT(entity_key) == SUM(cluster_size)).
  7. Connected-Component Completeness: 0 cross-cluster edges.
  8. Minimum-Label Determinism: resolved_id == MIN(entity_key) for every cluster.
  9. Golden Profile Bijectivity: Exactly 1 Golden Profile per cluster.
  10. MCP Latency Verification: Benchmarks all 17 MCP agent tools against the 260,000-entity graph (sub-second response times).

docs.title: 📈 Generating Custom Scale Datasets
docs.text:
To generate multi-million-row synthetic retail datasets:

# Generate 10 Million rows using Mimesis
python tools/scale_test/generate_retail_idr_mimesis.py \
  --config tools/scale_test/configs/retail_idr_10m.yaml

# Load into DuckDB
python tools/scale_test/load_duckdb.py \
  --input-dir tools/scale_test/output/retail_idr_10m \
  --db retail_10m.duckdb

# Or stage to Cloud Storage & load into Snowflake / BigQuery / Databricks
python tools/scale_test/load_snowflake.py --input-dir tools/scale_test/output/retail_idr_10m ...
python tools/scale_test/load_bigquery.py --input-dir tools/scale_test/output/retail_idr_10m ...
python tools/scale_test/load_databricks.py --input-dir tools/scale_test/output/retail_idr_10m ...

docs.text: Data Scale DuckDB Snowflake BigQuery Databricks < 1M rows In-Memory / File (4GB RAM) X-Small Warehouse On-Demand Serverless Small Serverless SQL Warehouse 10M rows 16GB RAM, Local NVMe (~140s) Medium Warehouse (~160s) Slot Reservation (~300s) Medium SQL Warehouse (~280s) 50M - 100M+ 64GB+ RAM Workstation Large / X-Large Warehouse Reservation + Partitioning Large SQL Warehouse / Photon

docs.title: Memory & Disk Tips:
docs.text:
• DuckDB: When running automated scale test suites locally, prefer conn = duckdb.connect(":memory:") to prevent temporary write amplification and disk full errors.
  • Delta Lake on Databricks: Use OPTIMIZE idr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current ZORDER BY (resolved_id) to cluster files for ultra-fast point lookups.

docs.title: Troubleshooting & Common Issues
docs.text: Solutions and diagnostic steps for common identity resolution and warehouse issues.

docs.title: Databricks: WRONG_COLUMN_DEFAULTS_FOR_DELTA_FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED
docs.text:
• Cause: Delta Lake tables by default require the table feature allowColumnDefaults to be enabled to accept column DEFAULT clauses.
  • Resolution: IDR's schema manager automatically suppresses DEFAULT clauses when creating Delta tables. If running custom DDL scripts, ensure column defaults are omitted from Delta CREATE TABLE statements or execute: 
    ALTER TABLE tableName SET TBLPROPERTIES('delta.feature.allowColumnDefaults' = 'supported');

docs.title: Databricks: Schema & Catalog Resolution
docs.text:
• Cause: Unity Catalog workspaces require queries to know the target catalog.
  • Resolution: Set export DATABRICKS_CATALOG="your_catalog" or configure default catalog in your warehouse settings.

docs.title: BigQuery: bigquery.datasets.delete permission denied
docs.text:
• Cause: When calling idr init --reset with BigQuery, dropping datasets requires roles/bigquery.dataOwner or bigquery.datasets.delete.
  • Resolution: Grant the service account roles/bigquery.dataOwner on the target project, or run idr init without --reset to alter/create tables in place without dropping the datasets.

docs.title: Snowflake: Query Timeout on Multi-Million Row Datasets
docs.text:
• Cause: An undersized warehouse (X-Small) running heavy initial full label propagation.
  • Resolution: Temporarily scale warehouse to Medium or Large for initial historical load: 
    ALTER WAREHOUSE COMPUTE_WH SET WAREHOUSE_SIZE = 'LARGE';

docs.title: DuckDB: Failed to create checkpoint ... No space left on device
docs.text:
• Cause: Generating very large synthetic datasets (e.g. 100k+ rows) in temporary file directories on full local partitions.
  • Resolution: Use duckdb.connect(":memory:") for test suites, or point --db to an external drive with adequate disk space.

docs.title: Giant Clusters & Graph Explosion
docs.text:
• Symptom: A single cluster contains thousands or millions of entities (e.g. cluster_size > 10000).
  • Cause: Common sentinel values like null, n/a, unknown@domain.com, or shared store tablet emails.
  • Resolution:

  • Add the problematic value to idr_meta.identifier_exclusion (or via the UI Setup Wizard Step 4): 

    INSERT INTO idr_meta.identifier_exclusion (identifier_type, identifier_value_pattern, match_type, reason)
VALUES ('email', 'shared_kiosk@store.com', 'EXACT', 'Shared store device');

  • Set max_group_size on the matching rule (e.g. 100 or 5000). Oversized groups will be automatically skipped and logged to idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups.

docs.title: Label Propagation Not Converging
docs.text:
• Symptom: Pipeline run completes with warning: Label propagation did not fully converge after 30 iterations.
  • Cause: Highly complex cyclical graph chains.
  • Resolution:

  • Increase max_iters: 

    idr run --platform [platform] --mode FULL --max-iters 50

  • Inspect idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups to check for unintentional hubs connecting disparate networks.

docs.title: Concurrent Run Lock / Stale Run Detected
docs.text:
• Symptom: PreflightStage fails with Concurrent run detected: run_....
  • Cause: A previous worker process crashed or was terminated while in RUNNING status.
  • Resolution: IDR automatically marks stale runs older than 4 hours as INTERRUPTED. To manually clear an active lock: 
    UPDATE idr_out.run_history
SET status = 'INTERRUPTED', error_message = 'Manually cleared'
WHERE status = 'RUNNING';

docs.title: Inspecting Execution Stage Telemetry
docs.text:
To diagnose where execution time was spent during a run: 

SELECT
    stage_name,
    stage_order,
    duration_seconds,
    rows_out
FROM idr_out.stage_metrics
WHERE run_id = 'your_run_id'
ORDER BY stage_order;

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text: Continuous integration and deployment pipelines for SQL Identity Resolution.

docs.title: Test Workflows
docs.text:
Automated testing on pull requests ensures stability across platforms.

# .github/workflows/test.yml
name: Test
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test-duckdb:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: '3.11'}
      - run: pip install duckdb pytest
      - run: python -m pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/legacy -v

docs.title: Package Smoke Gate
docs.text:
test.yml also builds wheel/sdist and installs from the built wheel before tests.

jobs:
  package-smoke:
    steps:
      - run: python -m build
      - run: twine check dist/*
      - run: |
          python -m venv .venv-smoke
          . .venv-smoke/bin/activate
          pip install dist/*.whl
          idr version

docs.title: Lockfile Enforcement
docs.text:
CI dependency installation uses pinned lockfiles:

  • requirements/ci.lock for test, lint, and DDL validation jobs
  • requirements/release.lock for package/release artifact jobs
  • requirements/docs.lock for docs workflow

UI dependencies are verified with npm ci to enforce idr_ui/package-lock.json.

docs.title: SBOM Verification
docs.text:
test.yml includes an sbom-verify job that:

  1. Builds Python artifacts (dist/*)
  2. Builds API and UI Docker images
  3. Generates SPDX JSON SBOMs for each artifact/image
  4. Verifies SBOM structure in CI using jq checks
  5. Uploads SBOMs as workflow artifacts

docs.title: Enterprise E2E Gate
docs.text:
test.yml includes enterprise-e2e that validates the enterprise stack end-to-end:

  1. Boots docker-compose.enterprise.yml
  2. Verifies Keycloak realm bootstrap
  3. Verifies API health and Prometheus health
  4. Confirms /metrics payload
  5. Confirms auth enforcement on protected endpoints
  6. Retrieves OIDC token and validates authenticated API access
  7. Verifies Prometheus target health for idr-api

docs.title: Release Workflow
docs.text:
release.yml is tag-driven (v*) and produces reproducible artifacts:

  • Python wheel + sdist
  • Wheel install smoke check
  • GHCR images for idr-api and idr-ui
  • Trivy vulnerability gating on dist artifacts and container images (fails on HIGH/CRITICAL)
  • Signed build provenance attestations for dist artifacts and pushed images

Manual runs are available through workflow_dispatch to optionally push images or publish package. Release summary includes an attestation link: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/attestations

docs.title: DDL Validation
docs.text:
Ensure SQL schema definitions are valid before merging.

# .github/workflows/validate-ddl.yml
name: Validate DDL
on:
  pull_request:
    paths: ['sql/**/*.sql']
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: pip install duckdb
      - run: |
          python -c "
          import duckdb
          conn = duckdb.connect(':memory:')
          with open('sql/ddl/duckdb.sql') as f:
              conn.execute(f.read())
          print('DuckDB DDL valid')
          "

# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/psf/black
    rev: 23.12.1
    hooks:
      - id: black
        language_version: python3.11

  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: validate-ddl
        name: Validate DuckDB DDL
        entry: python -c "import duckdb; duckdb.connect(':memory:').execute(open('sql/ddl/duckdb.sql').read())"
        language: python
        files: sql/ddl/.*\.sql$
        additional_dependencies: [duckdb]

docs.title: Snowflake

CREATE ROLE IDR_EXECUTOR;
-- Grant usage on warehouse and database
GRANT USAGE ON WAREHOUSE compute_wh TO ROLE IDR_EXECUTOR;
GRANT USAGE ON DATABASE analytics TO ROLE IDR_EXECUTOR;

-- Read-only on source data
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA crm TO ROLE IDR_EXECUTOR;

-- Full control of IDR schemas
GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA idr_meta TO ROLE IDR_EXECUTOR;
GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA idr_work TO ROLE IDR_EXECUTOR;
GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA idr_out TO ROLE IDR_EXECUTOR;

docs.text: System architecture, design patterns, and cross-platform data flow.

docs.title: High-Level Design
docs.text:
graph TB
    subgraph Ingestion["1. Ingestion & Extraction"]
        Sources[Source Tables: CRM, POS, Web] --> Extract[Extract & Normalize Identifiers / Attributes]
        Exclusions[Identifier Exclusions Blocklist] -.-> Extract
    end

    subgraph GraphBuilding["2. Identity Graph Formation"]
        Extract --> Edges[Anchor-Based Edge Building]
        Guardrails[max_group_size Safeguards] -.-> Edges
        Edges --> Skipped[idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups]
    end

    subgraph Resolution["3. Distributed Graph Resolution"]
        Edges --> LP[Set-Based SQL Label Propagation]
        LP --> Clusters[Connected-Component Cluster Assignment]
        Fuzzy[Optional Probabilistic Super-Clustering] -.-> Clusters
    end

    subgraph Output["4. Unified Customer 360 Output"]
        Clusters --> Members[idr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current]

docs.title: 1. Metadata Layer (idr_meta)
docs.text:
• Source Registry (source_table): Registered source tables with primary keys, watermark columns, and lookback windows.
  • Rule Definitions (rule, fuzzy_rule): Exact matching rules and probabilistic fuzzy similarity rules.
  • Mappings (identifier_mapping, entity_attribute_mapping): Column-to-identifier and column-to-profile mappings.
  • Survivorship Policies (survivorship_rule): Declarative resolution strategies (RECENCY, PRIORITY, FREQUENCY).
  • Safety Lists (identifier_exclusion): Exact and wildcard blocklists for false-linkage prevention.
  • Watermark State (run_state): Tracks high-watermark timestamps for incremental delta processing.

docs.title: 2. Processing & Staging Layer (idr_work)
docs.text:
• Transient State: Staging tables created and dropped per run (entities_delta, identifiers_all, edges_new, lp_labels, cluster_attributes).
  • Incremental Efficiency: In INCR mode, only updated source records and their direct neighborhood in the identity graph are extracted into idr_work.

docs.title: 3. Output Layer (idr_out)
docs.text:
• Resolved Membership (identity_resolved_membership_current): Maps each source entity to its canonical resolved_id.
  • Cluster Registry (identity_clusters_current): Master list of clusters with size, confidence score, and primary reason.
  • Golden Records (golden_profiles): Unified customer 360 profile table with resolved survivorship attributes.
  • Active Edges (identity_edges_current): Direct pairwise edges with evidence rules and observation timestamps.
  • Identifier Registry (identity_identifiers_current): Active registry enabling fast single-hop candidate expansion in incremental mode.
  • Audit Trails (run_history, stage_metrics, config_snapshot): Full telemetry capturing run status, per-stage durations, and configuration hashes.

docs.title: Cross-Platform Execution Architecture
docs.text:
The core IDR engine is written in pure, dialect-aware SQL generated by idr_core:

  • DuckDB: Executes in-process using vectorized execution, ideal for local development, CI/CD, and embedded edge workloads.
  • Snowflake: Runs in-warehouse via standard SQL or Snowpark sessions, leveraging micro-partition pruning and virtual warehouse scaling.
  • BigQuery: Serverless parallel processing leveraging DDL/DML, partition pruning, and string similarity functions.
  • Databricks: Runs natively on Spark SQL / Delta Lake across Serverless SQL Warehouses and Unity Catalog, leveraging Photon acceleration.

docs.title: Matching Algorithm & Graph Resolution
docs.text: SQL Identity Resolution uses a deterministic-first, graph-native approach to entity linkage. By executing connected component analysis directly within standard SQL engines, it eliminates the need for specialized graph databases or external SaaS tools while maintaining formal mathematical guarantees of partition completeness.

docs.title: 📐 Algorithm Overview
docs.text:
The resolution engine operates in two principal phases:

flowchart TD
    subgraph Phase1["Phase 1: Deterministic Matching (Strict)"]
        Extract["1. PII Extraction & Normalization<br/>(Cleanse email, phone, IDs)"]
        Excl["2. Guardrail Filtering<br/>(Exclude blocklisted & high-cardinality groups)"]
        Edges["3. Anchor-Based Edge Building<br/>(N-1 star graph: O(N) edges)"]
        LP["4. Distributed Label Propagation<br/>(Iterative SQL transitive closure)"]
    end

    subgraph Phase2["Phase 2: Probabilistic Refinement (Optional)"]
        Block["5. Candidate Blocking<br/>(Metaphone / Phonetic grouping)"]
        Score["6. Similarity Scoring<br/>(Jaro-Winkler / Levenshtein)"]
        Merge["7. Cluster Merging<br/>(Score >= Threshold)"]
    end

    subgraph Output["Phase 3: Golden Profile Survivorship"]
        Surv["8. Attribute Selection<br/>(Recency, Source Priority, Most Frequent)"]
    end

    Extract --> Excl --> Edges --> LP
    LP --> Block --> Score --> Merge
    Merge --> Surv

docs.title: 1. Extraction & Normalization
docs.text:
Source tables (e.g. crm.contacts, ecom.orders, mobile.users) contain raw identity signals. During the Extraction Stage:

  1. Mapping Rules: Each rule in idr_meta.identifier_mapping extracts specific columns or expressions.
  2. Normalization Functions:
  3. Email: Lowercased, leading/trailing whitespace removed, common aliases stripped.
  4. Phone: Stripped of non-digit characters (+, -, ( )), formatted to E.164 or national 10-digit standard.
  5. Custom Expression: Supports warehouse-native SQL expressions (e.g., TRIM(UPPER(loyalty_num))).
  6. Hashing: Normalised identifier values are hashed (SHA-256) into identifier_hash for uniform indexing and anonymized internal processing.

docs.title: 2. Guardrails & Cardinality Protections
docs.text:
A common pitfall in identity resolution is "cluster explosion"—a shared identifier (like support@company.com, 000-000-0000, or a shared office phone) linking hundreds of thousands of unrelated individuals into a massive "super-cluster".

sql-identity-oss enforces two layers of cardinality protection:

docs.title: Exact & Wildcard Blocklists (idr_meta.identifier_exclusion)
docs.text:
Before any edges are formed, identifiers are checked against an exclusion registry:

  • Exact match: Excludes placeholder emails like test@test.com, unknown@gmail.com.
  • Domain wildcard: Excludes high-volume corporate email addresses or common generic domains.

docs.title: Group Size Capping (max_group_size)
docs.text:
Every rule specifies a max_group_size (default: 50):

  • If an identifier matches $N > \text{max_group_size}$ distinct entities, the group is not linked.
  • Instead, it is routed to idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups with the reason EXCEEDS_MAX_GROUP_SIZE.
  • This ensures that edge generation runtime and memory footprint remain deterministic and sub-linear.

docs.title: 3. Anchor-Based Edge Building ($O(N)$ vs $O(N^2)$)
docs.text:
Traditional entity resolution connects all pairs within an identifier group, creating a complete graph $K_N$:

$$\text{Edges}_{\text{complete}} = \frac{N(N - 1)}{2} \in O(N^2)$$

For a group of 1,000 records, a complete graph creates 499,500 edges.

Instead, sql-identity-oss employs Anchor-Based Edge Construction:

  1. Within each identifier group, the entity with the lowest lexicographical entity_key is designated as the Anchor.
  2. Directed or undirected edges are formed exclusively between each member and the anchor:

$$\text{Edges}_{\text{anchor}} = N - 1 \in O(N)$$

Complete Graph (O(N^2))            Anchor Graph (O(N))
      A --- B                            A (Anchor)
      |  X  |                           / | \
      C --- D                          B  C  D
  (6 edges for 4 nodes)          (3 edges for 4 nodes)

Because connected component reachability is transitive ($B \sim A \land C \sim A \implies B \sim C$), the anchor star graph preserves exact topological connectivity while drastically reducing edge volume.

docs.title: 4. SQL-Native Label Propagation
docs.text:
Connected components are resolved using an iterative SQL technique called Label Propagation:

  1. Initialization: Every entity starts with its own entity_key as its initial cluster label.

  2. Propagation Step: In each iteration $k$, every node queries all its immediate neighbors across the edge table and adopts the minimum label: $$\text{Label}{v}^{(k+1)} = \min \left( \text{Label} \right)$$}^{(k)}, \min_{u \in \text{Neighbors}(v)} \text{Label}_{u}^{(k)

  3. Convergence: The algorithm tracks the number of nodes whose label changed during the iteration.

  4. If $\Delta = 0$, the graph has reached a fixed-point equilibrium: all nodes in each connected component share the identical minimum resolved_id.
  5. Execution terminates automatically or halts when max_lp_iterations (default: 30) is reached.
  6. Monotonicity Guarantee: Labels only ever decrease ($\text{Label}^{(k+1)} \le \text{Label}^{(k)}$). Because the label space is finite and bounded below by the minimum node ID in the component, convergence is mathematically guaranteed.

docs.title: 5. Probabilistic Refinement (Optional)
docs.text:
When strict deterministic matching is completed, an optional fuzzy matching stage (--strict=false) can resolve near-matches:

  1. Blocking: Candidates are partitioned into narrow blocks using blocking keys (e.g., soundex/metaphone of last name + zip code prefix).
  2. Fuzzy Scoring: For candidates within the same block, string similarity metrics are computed:
  3. Jaro-Winkler for names.
  4. Levenshtein / Damerau-Levenshtein for alphanumeric codes.
  5. Merge Evaluation: If the similarity score exceeds the configured confidence_threshold (e.g., 0.85), an edge is materialized and merged into the cluster.

docs.title: 6. Golden Profile Survivorship
docs.text:
Once clusters (resolved_id) are formed, the Output Stage consolidates all associated entity records into a single canonical Golden Customer Profile using configurable survivorship rules:

Survivorship Rule Description Common Use Case MOST_RECENT Selects attribute value from the entity with the latest updated_at timestamp Current residential address, preferred phone SOURCE_PRIORITY Prioritizes authoritative sources (e.g., Billing CRM > Marketing Web Form) Legal first name, legal last name MOST_FREQUENT Selects the statistical mode across all linked records Gender, locale, timezone AGGREGATE_ARRAY Aggregates all unique values across records into an array All historical email addresses, past loyalty IDs NON_NULL_FALLBACK Picks the first non-null value according to source priority Secondary phone, company name

All survivorship decisions are written to idr_out.golden_customer_profiles, accompanied by the cluster's aggregate confidence score and size metrics.

docs.title: Data Model & Schema Architecture
docs.text: SQL Identity Resolution is structured around a three-tier schema architecture designed for high-concurrency warehouses, transactional isolation, and complete auditability.

docs.title: 🏛️ Three-Tier Schema Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph MetaSchema["1. Configuration & Rules (idr_meta)"]
        IM["identifier_mapping<br/>(Source extraction rules)"]
        IE["identifier_exclusion<br/>(Blocklisted values & wildcards)"]
        SR["survivorship_rules<br/>(Golden profile precedence)"]
        RC["run_control<br/>(State, watermark & iteration bounds)"]
    end

    subgraph WorkSchema["2. Transient Pipeline State (idr_work)"]
        ENT["entities_work<br/>(Extracted entity rows)"]
        IDN["identifiers_work<br/>(Normalized & hashed PII)"]
        EDG["edges_work<br/>(Anchor-based graph edges)"]
        LP["label_propagation_work<br/>(Iterative cluster state)"]
    end

    subgraph OutSchema["3. Serving & Analytics (idr_out)"]
        CLUST["identity_clusters_current<br/>(Active resolved clusters)"]
        MEMB["identity_resolved_membership_current<br/>(Entity -> Cluster mapping)"]
        GOLD["golden_customer_profiles<br/>(Consolidated golden records)"]
        AUD["identity_run_audit<br/>(Lineage, run metrics & timing)"]
    end

    MetaSchema --> WorkSchema
    WorkSchema --> OutSchema

docs.title: 1. Metadata Schema (idr_meta)
docs.text: Stores rule definitions, source mappings, attribute priority matrices, and pipeline configuration. Changes to this schema take effect on the next pipeline execution.

docs.title: Key Tables:
docs.text:
• identifier_mapping: Defines which columns from source tables contain identifiers (e.g., EMAIL, PHONE, ACCOUNT_ID), the extraction SQL expression, and the max_group_size threshold.
  • identifier_exclusion: Contains exact match strings (e.g. test@example.com, 0000000000) and wildcard patterns that must be filtered out before graph construction.
  • survivorship_rules: Configures rule priority (SOURCE_PRIORITY, MOST_RECENT, MOST_FREQUENT) on an attribute-by-attribute basis for constructing golden customer profiles.
  • run_control: Tracks execution parameters, incremental watermarks, and convergence tolerances.

docs.title: 2. Working Schema (idr_work)
docs.text: Isolated workspace used during pipeline execution. In INCR mode, only affected subgraphs and delta entities are processed in this tier, leaving production serving tables untouched until commitment.

docs.title: Key Tables:
docs.text:
• entities_work: Entity keys extracted from source records with primary source timestamps and system origins.
  • identifiers_work: Extracted PII values after case normalization, whitespace trimming, regex cleansing, and cryptographic hashing.
  • edges_work: The materialized graph edges formed between entities. In strict deterministic mode, this table contains star-topology anchor edges connecting entities sharing identical identifiers.
  • label_propagation_work: Working table storing the current cluster label assignments during iterative SQL execution. Tracks label delta counts after each step until $\Delta = 0$.

docs.title: 3. Output Schema (idr_out)
docs.text: The consumption and serving layer queried by downstream analytics, Reverse ETL, Customer Data Platforms (CDPs), CRM syncs, and BI tools.

docs.title: Key Tables:
docs.text:
• identity_clusters_current: One row per distinct real-world entity / customer cluster:
  • resolved_id: Primary key of the resolved entity.
  • cluster_size: Number of distinct records grouped into this cluster.
  • confidence_score: Weighted confidence calculation (0.00 to 1.00) based on identifier quality.
  • created_at / updated_at: Cluster lifecycle timestamps.
  • identity_resolved_membership_current: Fast lookup table mapping every source record to its resolved identity:
  • entity_key: Unique record key (source_system:source_pck).
  • resolved_id: Canonical cluster identifier.
  • is_anchor: Boolean indicating whether this entity serves as the cluster's anchor.
  • golden_customer_profiles: The unified customer record created by applying survivorship rules across all linked entities:
  • Canonical names, primary email, primary phone, postal address.
  • Unified identifiers array (e.g. all known emails or device tokens associated with this person).
  • identity_run_audit: Granular execution log recording run mode (FULL vs INCR), stage timings, input row counts, edges materialized, clusters resolved, and convergence iteration counts.
  • skipped_identifier_groups: Audit table documenting identifier values that exceeded max_group_size or matched exclusion filters, preserving data quality observability.

docs.title: How It Works: An Intuitive Guide
docs.text:
Identity resolution can sound complex, but its core principle is simple: connecting fragmented records that belong to the exact same real-world individual or household.

This guide explains how sql-identity-oss resolves identity records step-by-step using an intuitive business card analogy.

docs.title: 📇 The Business Card Analogy
docs.text:
Imagine a shoebox filled with mixed-up business cards collected across different company touchpoints:

[ Card A: In-Store POS ]
Name:  "John Smith"
Email: john.smith@gmail.com
Phone: (not provided)

[ Card B: Web Checkout ]
Name:  "J. Smith"
Email: john.smith@gmail.com
Phone: (555) 019-2834

[ Card C: Mobile App ]
Name:  "Johnny S."
Email: (not provided)
Phone: 555-019-2834
Device: iOS-UUID-88912

At first glance, a naive database query cannot link Card A to Card C because they share no attributes in common (Card A only has an email, Card C only has a phone and device ID).

Here is how SQL Identity Resolution connects them deterministically in standard SQL:

docs.title: Step 1: PII Cleansing & Normalization
docs.text:
Raw data is notoriously inconsistent—casing differs, phones have dashes or parentheses, and whitespace creeps in.

The engine normalizes all extracted identifiers into uniform tokens:

  • john.smith@gmail.com -> john.smith@gmail.com (lowercased)
  • (555) 019-2834 -> 5550192834 (digits only)
  • 555-019-2834 -> 5550192834 (digits only)

docs.title: Step 2: Direct Match Linking (Card A ↔ Card B)
docs.text:
Card A and Card B both possess john.smith@gmail.com. The engine creates a link (graph edge) between Card A and Card B.

[ Card A ] <====== EMAIL: john.smith@gmail.com ======> [ Card B ]

docs.title: Step 3: Transitive Chaining (Card B ↔ Card C)
docs.text:
Card B also contains phone 5550192834. Card C also contains phone 5550192834. The engine creates a link between Card B and Card C.

[ Card A ] <==== EMAIL ====> [ Card B ] <==== PHONE ====> [ Card C ]

docs.title: Step 4: Connected Components via Label Propagation
docs.text:
Now we have a chain: $$\text{Card A} \longleftrightarrow \text{Card B} \longleftrightarrow \text{Card C}$$

Through transitive closure, because A is linked to B, and B is linked to C, A, B, and C all belong to the same person.

The engine assigns all three records the same canonical cluster identifier: $$\text{resolved_id} = \text{"RES-882014"}$$

docs.title: Step 5: Constructing the Golden Customer Record
docs.text:
With the cluster established, survivorship rules merge the best pieces of information from each card into one master profile:

{
  "resolved_id": "RES-882014",
  "golden_name": "John Smith",
  "primary_email": "john.smith@gmail.com",
  "primary_phone": "5550192834",
  "known_devices": ["iOS-UUID-88912"],
  "sources_linked": ["in_store_pos", "web_checkout", "mobile_app"],
  "record_count": 3,
  "confidence_score": 0.98
}

docs.title: ⚡ What Makes This Engine Different?
docs.text: Traditional CDP / SaaS SQL Identity Resolution (sql-identity-oss) Data Leaves Warehouse: PII is copied to third-party SaaS cloud. Zero Data Egress: 100% executes inside DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks. Black-Box Scoring: Opaque machine learning algorithms merge records unexpectedly. 100% Deterministic & Auditable: Every edge is traced to a rule and exact identifier match. Expensive SaaS Pricing: Pay-per-profile subscriptions that scale exponentially. Open-Source & Cloud-Native: Compute scales linearly with warehouse credits. Separate Graph Infrastructure: Requires hosting and maintaining Neo4j or Amazon Neptune. Pure SQL Execution: Runs directly using warehouse SQL and relational tables.
