docs.title: Warehouse Sizing & Capacity Planning
docs.text: SQL Identity Resolution executes graph algorithms and table merges directly inside your data warehouse engine. This guide provides concrete hardware and warehouse sizing recommendations across all 4 supported platforms based on production benchmarks.

docs.title: 📊 Sizing Matrix by Platform & Record Volume
docs.text: Platform < 100K Records 1M Records 10M Records 50M - 100M+ Records DuckDB In-Memory / 2GB RAM 4 Cores, 8GB RAM 8 Cores, 32GB RAM 16 Cores, 64GB-128GB RAM (NVMe disk) Snowflake X-Small X-Small - Small Medium - Large X-Large - 2X-Large BigQuery On-demand (default) On-demand (default) 500-1,000 slots 2,000+ slots (Reservations) Databricks Serverless SQL / Small 2-4 Workers (Standard) 4-8 Workers (Standard) 8-16 Workers (Photon-enabled)

docs.title: 🦆 DuckDB (Local / Single Node)
docs.text: DuckDB handles millions of records on standard developer laptops and single cloud compute instances (e.g., AWS c6i.4xlarge or GCP c2-standard-16).

docs.title: Memory & Storage Recommendations:
docs.text:
• Memory: Reserve roughly 1.5GB RAM per million entity records.
  • Storage: DuckDB uses columnar compression. A database storing 10M customer rows and 30M extracted identifiers typically occupies 3GB - 6GB of disk space.
  • Threads: DuckDB defaults to utilizing all available CPU cores. For batch CLI workloads, keep default threading enabled.

docs.title: ❄️ Snowflake
docs.text: Snowflake's columnar engine excels at join-heavy graph edge generation and recursive label propagation.

docs.title: Warehouse Recommendations:
docs.text:
• Initial Setup / POC (< 1M records): X-Small warehouse provides ample capacity and minimizes credit consumption.
  • Production Daily Batch (5M - 20M records): Medium warehouse typically completes full resolution in 4 to 8 minutes.
  • Large Scale (50M - 100M+ records): Use X-Large or 2X-Large.
  • Auto-Suspend: Set auto-suspend to 60 seconds so compute costs cease immediately after pipeline completion: 
    ALTER WAREHOUSE idr_wh SET AUTO_SUSPEND = 60 AUTO_RESUME = TRUE;

docs.title: 🔍 Google Cloud BigQuery
docs.text: BigQuery provides serverless execution where compute automatically scales based on query complexity.

docs.title: Configuration Best Practices:
docs.text:
• On-Demand vs Reservations:
  • For datasets < 10M rows, BigQuery's On-Demand pricing ($6.25 per TB scanned) is cost-effective because query filtering and column pruning keep scanned bytes low.
  • For recurring enterprise production runs (> 50M records), BigQuery Slots (Capacity Reservations) provide predictable pricing and prevent concurrency throttling.
  • Partitioning & Clustering:
  • Cluster idr_work.identifiers_work by (identifier_type, identifier_hash).
  • Cluster idr_work.edges_work by (identifier_type, src_key).
  • This reduces slot runtime during join operations by up to 60%.

docs.title: 🧱 Databricks (Spark & Delta Lake)
docs.text: Databricks leverages Apache Spark and Photon to distribute graph resolution across multi-node clusters.

docs.title: Spark Configuration for Large Datasets (> 10M records):
docs.text:
When running on Databricks clusters or Lakeflow jobs, apply the following Spark configurations:

# Enable Adaptive Query Execution for dynamic shuffle partitions
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")

# Tune shuffle partitions based on cluster worker cores
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "800")

# Delta Lake optimizations
spark.conf.set("spark.databricks.delta.optimizeWrite.enabled", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.databricks.delta.autoCompact.enabled", "true")

docs.title: Table Properties:
docs.text:
For Delta tables in Databricks Unity Catalog, enable column defaults and auto-compaction: 

ALTER TABLE idr_out.identity_clusters_current
SET TBLPROPERTIES (
    'delta.feature.allowColumnDefaults' = 'supported',
    'delta.autoOptimize.optimizeWrite' = 'true',
    'delta.autoOptimize.autoCompact' = 'true'
);

docs.title: Scaling Strategies & High-Volume Operations
docs.text: Scaling identity resolution to tens or hundreds of millions of entities introduces unique graph and database challenges. This guide outlines battle-tested architectural strategies to process high-volume workloads reliably and cost-effectively.

docs.title: Problem A: The Supernode Phenomenon
docs.text:
A "supernode" occurs when an identifier is shared across a massive number of records. Common real-world examples:

  • Placeholder emails: test@test.com, noemail@store.com, guest@checkout.com
  • Default phone numbers: 000-000-0000, 123-456-7890, company switchboards
  • Null or empty strings that bypassed ingestion validation

If an identifier is shared by 100,000 records, building an unconstrained clique creates: $$\frac{100,000 \times 99,999}{2} \approx 5 \text{ Billion Edges}$$

This will exhaust warehouse memory, cause query spills, and merge unrelated customers into a single gargantuan cluster.

docs.title: Solutions in sql-identity-oss:
docs.text:
1. max_group_size Thresholding: Set per-rule in idr_meta.identifier_mapping (default: 50). Groups exceeding this size are safely bypassed from edge formation and logged to idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups.
  2. Exclusion Registry: Maintain exact and domain wildcard exclusions in idr_meta.identifier_exclusion.
  3. Anchor Topology: Even within allowed groups ($N \le 50$), only $N - 1$ edges are formed instead of $N(N - 1) / 2$.

docs.title: Problem B: Deep Linear Chains & Convergence Latency
docs.text: When individuals share intermediate devices or addresses across extended time periods, long chains can emerge ($A \leftrightarrow B \leftrightarrow C \leftrightarrow \dots \leftrightarrow Z$). In naive label propagation, propagating the minimum label through a chain of diameter $D$ requires $D$ iterative SQL steps.

docs.title: Solutions:
docs.text:
1. Tune max_lp_iterations: The default is 30 iterations. Most enterprise datasets converge in 4 to 8 iterations. If iteration counts consistently approach 30, investigate whether false-positive linkages (e.g. shared family phones or retail store devices) are creating artificial bridges.
  2. Bi-directional Edge Doubling: Edges are evaluated symmetrically (src -> dst and dst -> src), ensuring labels propagate in both directions concurrently and halving the required steps to span a chain.

docs.title: 🔄 2. Incremental Mode (--mode INCR)
docs.text:
Running full identity resolution (FULL mode) across 100M records daily is compute-inefficient. Instead, use Incremental Resolution:

idr run --platform snowflake --mode INCR

docs.title: How Incremental Mode Works:
docs.text:
1. Delta Entity Identification: Inspects source tables using high-watermark timestamps (updated_at > last_successful_run_at).
  2. Impacted Subgraph Discovery: Identifies all existing entities and clusters that share identifiers with the incoming delta entities.
  3. Localized Label Propagation: Re-evaluates label propagation only within the impacted connected components.
  4. Target Table Merge: Uses atomic warehouse MERGE INTO statements to update identity_clusters_current and identity_resolved_membership_current without touching unaffected clusters.

Impact: In typical production retail environments where 2-5% of profiles change daily, incremental mode reduces processed edge volume by 90-95%, cutting runtime and warehouse credits by up to 80%.

docs.title: 🗄️ 3. Physical Storage & Clustering Optimization
docs.text: When tables in idr_work and idr_out exceed 100GB, optimize warehouse physical layout:

docs.title: Snowflake
docs.text:
ALTER TABLE idr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current
CLUSTER BY (resolved_id, entity_key);

ALTER TABLE idr_out.identity_clusters_current
CLUSTER BY (resolved_id);

docs.text:
-- Partition by extraction date and cluster by hash
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE idr_work.identifiers_work
PARTITION BY DATE(extracted_at)
CLUSTER BY identifier_type, identifier_hash;

docs.title: Databricks
docs.text:
OPTIMIZE idr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current
ZORDER BY (resolved_id, entity_key);

docs.title: Production Hardening
docs.text: Best practices for running SQL Identity Resolution in production environments.

docs.title: max_group_size
docs.text:
Prevents generic identifiers from creating mega-clusters.

-- Set appropriate limits
UPDATE idr_meta.rule SET max_group_size = 10000 WHERE identifier_type = 'EMAIL';
UPDATE idr_meta.rule SET max_group_size = 5000 WHERE identifier_type = 'PHONE';
UPDATE idr_meta.rule SET max_group_size = 1 WHERE identifier_type = 'SSN';

What happens when exceeded:

  1. Identifier group is skipped
  2. Entities become singletons (resolved_id = entity_key)
  3. Logged to idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups

docs.title: Identifier Exclusions
docs.text:
Block known bad identifiers:

-- Exact matches
INSERT INTO idr_meta.identifier_exclusion VALUES
  ('EMAIL', 'test@test.com', FALSE, 'Generic test'),
  ('EMAIL', 'null@null.com', FALSE, 'Null placeholder'),
  ('PHONE', '0000000000', FALSE, 'Invalid');

-- Patterns (LIKE syntax)
INSERT INTO idr_meta.identifier_exclusion VALUES
  ('EMAIL', '%@example.com', TRUE, 'Example domain'),
  ('EMAIL', 'noreply@%', TRUE, 'No-reply');

docs.title: Alerting
docs.text:
Run warnings appear in idr_out.run_history:

SELECT run_id, status, large_clusters, groups_skipped, warnings
FROM idr_out.run_history
WHERE status = 'SUCCESS_WITH_WARNINGS'
ORDER BY started_at DESC;

docs.title: Use INCR Mode
docs.text:
After initial FULL run, use INCR for efficiency:

idr run --platform [platform] --mode FULL

# Subsequent runs
idr run --platform [platform] --mode INCR

CREATE INDEX idx_customers_email ON customers(LOWER(email));

-- Snowflake (clustering)

-- BigQuery (partitioning)

PARTITION BY DATE(updated_at)

docs.text:
Retrieve your Google Cloud BigQuery project information:

Parameter Type Where to Find in Google Cloud Console Example Value BIGQUERY_PROJECT_ID Identifier Top navigation project switcher in GCP Console my-data-project-123 BIGQUERY_DATASET Dataset Target dataset under your project ecommerce_demo BIGQUERY_LOCATION Region Dataset processing location (defaults to US) US or europe-west1

docs.title: B. Authentication & Zero-Retype Auto-Discovery (New in v0.6.1)
docs.text:
SQL Identity Resolution natively detects Google Cloud Application Default Credentials (ADC):

  1. Option 1: Google Cloud CLI (Recommended for Local Dev) Run this single command in your terminal: 

    gcloud auth application-default login
    This writes credentials to ~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json. The IDR Setup Wizard automatically detects your active GCP Project and presents a "Discovered Local Credentials" card with 1-Click Connect.

  2. Option 2: Service Account Key (Production / CI) Generate a Service Account Key JSON with BigQuery Admin or BigQuery Data Editor + BigQuery Job User roles: 

    export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/path/to/sa-key.json"
export IDR_PROJECT="my-data-project-123"

  3. Option 3: dbt Profiles If you have a ~/.dbt/profiles.yml with a BigQuery target, IDR auto-detects the project, dataset, and keyfile path.

docs.title: 💡 Troubleshooting & Gotchas
docs.text:
Compute Cold Starts & 503 Service Unavailable

Databricks Free Tier compute (SQL Warehouse or Community Cluster) auto-terminates after 20 minutes of inactivity. If a query or API call fails with Connection refused or 503 Service Unavailable, open your Databricks workspace and verify that the compute is in Running state.

Delta Lake Column Defaults

Databricks Delta Lake requires explicit feature flag activation for column defaults on certain classic runtime clusters. IDR automatically suppresses invalid default clauses in DDL to ensure table creation succeeds seamlessly across all cluster types.

Unity Catalog vs Hive Metastore Paths
  • If using Unity Catalog, tables are addressed as <catalog>.<schema>.<table> (e.g. main.idr_out.golden_customer_profiles).
  • If using Community Edition, set DATABRICKS_CATALOG="hive_metastore".
